newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SDP WANTS JOBS AS KEY FOCUS IN 1998 BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SDP WANTS JOBS AS KEY FOCUS IN 1998 BUDGET.

text.p: The Finnish Social Democratic Party (SDP) said on Thursday that economic policy should focus on stable growth, and that decisions in the 1998 state budget should consider particularly the effects on employment.
In the current cyclical situation it made sense to improve the shape of the state finances, the executive board of the party said in a statement.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen is chairman of SDP. He is scheduled to hold a news conference at 1400/1100 GMT on the coming autumn's political agenda.
"The main economic policy obejctive ... must be stable growth and, based on that, improved employment and securing citizens' purchasing power," SDP said.
Due to cyclical reasons, it was wise to use the room to manoeuver achieved during this government's term in office "to improve the shape of the state finances," the party said.

Each percentage point fall in the rate of unemployment was reducing the deficit of the state finances by two billion markka on an annual level, SDP said. "When deciding on the ... 1998 state budget proposal, particular attention must be paid to the employment effects," it added.
